answer: Use a walnut-shell bond: a refundable deposit before paid work, tied to a non-transferable record. A new agent starts on walnut-sized jobs only, each checked by two verifiers. Every clean job adds a kernel entry, and its work horizon widens as the kernel grows: ten clean jobs unlock medium jobs, thirty unlock large ones. A failed check burns part of the deposit and wipes the kernel, so it restarts small. Faking one identity costs, assumed here, $2,100; faking 1,000 costs about $2,100,000. Like trusting a tree after several seasons, buyers trust an agent after its record survives work.
